name: CARE
question: Does adding a standardized Burch colposuspension to abdominal sacrocolpopexy reduce postoperative stress incontinence in women who are stress-continent before surgery?

design.blinding: participants, research staff and telephone interviewers masked for at least 3 months

arms.label: Abdominal sacrocolpopexy with standardized Burch colposuspension

design.population: Women with stage II–IV prolapse who answered never or rarely to six stress-incontinence questions, whose urethrovesical junction mobility allowed a Burch colposuspension, and who chose open abdominal sacrocolpopexy at Pelvic Floor Disorders Network centers.
design.description: Multicenter, masked surgical randomized superiority trial
design.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1559–1561 (Methods); Fig. 2, p1560 (arm counts)

verdictNote: Benefit persisted to 7 years, though estimated stress incontinence still reached 62% with Burch versus 77% without.
takeaway: In stress-continent women having open abdominal sacrocolpopexy for prolapse, adding a standardized Burch colposuspension lowered the composite rate of stress incontinence at 3 months (33.6% versus 57.4%) without a significant difference in urge symptoms; enrollment stopped at the first interim analysis.

reports.label: Three-month randomized report
reports.citation: Brubaker L, Cundiff GW, Fine P, et al. Abdominal sacrocolpopexy with Burch colposuspension to reduce urinary stress incontinence. *N Engl J Med.* 2006;354(15):1557-1566. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa054208
reports.followUpLocator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1560–1561 (primary outcomes at 3 months); Fig. 2, p1560

results.measure: Stress incontinence at 3 months: any of symptoms, positive stress test or treatment (composite), corrected values
results.note: OR adjusted for surgeon and paravaginal repair; P adjusted for the same. Prespecified stopping level at the first interim analysis was 0.0042 (0.019 at the second), with 232 women having outcomes; the plan was 480 women to detect a 10-percentage-point difference. The endpoint could not be determined in 11 Burch and 10 control women, and three intention-to-treat sensitivity analyses stayed significant. The 2016 correction replaced the printed 35/147 (23.8%) and 67/152 (44.1%).
results.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1560–1561 and Table 3, p1565; correction N Engl J Med 2016;374:2297

results.measure: Stress incontinence component: yes to any of three PFDI stress items at 3 months
results.note: P adjusted for surgeon and paravaginal repair.

results.measure: Stress incontinence component: leakage on standardized stress test at maximal capacity or 300 mL at 3 months, corrected values
results.note: The 2016 correction (stress-test coding error) replaced the printed 7/148 (4.7%) and 14/162 (8.6%), P = 0.14.
results.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1565, Table 3; correction N Engl J Med 2016;374:2297

results.measure: Stress incontinence component: any treatment for stress incontinence after study surgery at 3 months
Bothersome stress incontinence at 3 months (moderately or quite a bit on the PFDI)
MESA score for stress incontinence at 3 months (mean ± SD; maximum 27)
Urge outcome at 3 months: any bothersome urge incontinence, urgency, frequency, nocturia or enuresis, or treatment for these
results.note: Methods list urge symptoms with stress incontinence as primary outcomes (p1560), but the null hypothesis concerned stress incontinence only. Bothersome components, Burch versus control: urge incontinence 10/147 (6.8%) vs 18/151 (11.9%), P = 0.18; frequency 17/153 vs 16/152, P = 0.74; urgency 9/153 vs 14/152, P = 0.52; nocturia 24/153 vs 21/152, P = 0.53; enuresis 0/153 vs 1/152, P = 0.50.
results.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1560 (definition); Table 3, p1565

results.measure: Treatment for urge symptoms after surgery, at 3 months, corrected values
results.note: The 2016 correction replaced the printed 2/153 (1.3%) and 5/152 (3.3%), P = 0.27.
results.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1565, Table 3; correction N Engl J Med 2016;374:2297

results.measure: MESA score for urge symptoms at 3 months (mean ± SD; maximum 18)

results.endpoint: Stress incontinence without leakage on prolapse reduction
results.measure: Composite stress incontinence at 3 months in women with no leakage on preoperative urodynamic prolapse reduction
results.note: Reported in the text as data not shown. The Burch effect appeared regardless of reduction-test result.

results.endpoint: Stress incontinence excluding baseline stress symptoms
results.measure: Composite stress incontinence at 3 months after excluding women with baseline PFDI stress symptoms
results.note: Concomitant paravaginal repair did not significantly change postoperative stress incontinence rates in either group.

harms.label: Serious adverse events to 3 months, all events
Serious adverse events judged plausibly related to the Burch surgery
harms.locator: N Engl J Med 2006;354:1565, Table 3; p1563
harms.note: P = 0.24. Three investigators independent of the sites and unaware of assignment judged relatedness.

harms.label: Urologic and gynecologic serious adverse events to 3 months
Urinary retention at 3 months
harms.note: Counts of women; described as rare.

delivery.label: Women randomized
delivery.note: 322 randomized of 1460 assessed (817 did not meet inclusion criteria, 181 declined, 111 excluded for other reasons, 29 consented but were not randomized, 14 of them because enrollment stopped). 480 were planned; enrollment stopped after the first interim analysis.

delivery.label: Received assigned intervention
delivery.note: All 322 were followed to the 3-month endpoint; the 3-month visit was completed by 147 and 163, and quality-of-life questionnaires by 152 and 150.

delivery.label: Operative time, incision to skin closure
Paravaginal repair planned before randomization
delivery.note: Plans changed in 2 women with Burch and 6 without.

delivery.label: Stress symptoms on PFDI at baseline
delivery.note: All women answered never or rarely to the six MESA stress items at screening; 19.2% reported stress leakage on the PFDI telephone interview.

delivery.label: Positive preoperative stress test without prolapse reduction
delivery.note: P = 0.09. Stress test at maximal cystometric capacity or 300 mL, whichever came first.

delivery.label: Positive preoperative stress test with prolapse reduction
delivery.note: Detrusor overactivity with or without urodynamic stress incontinence: 19/157 (12.1%) and 17/163 (10.4%).

delivery.label: Masking breaks before the 3-month visit
delivery.value: Assignment revealed to study coordinators in 5 women and to the women themselves in 2; surgeons learned preoperative urodynamic results in 2
delivery.note: Assignment was concealed in sealed opaque envelopes opened in the operating room after anesthesia.

reports.label: Preoperative urodynamics with prolapse reduction
reports.citation: Visco AG, Brubaker L, Nygaard I, et al. The role of preoperative urodynamic testing in stress-continent women undergoing sacrocolpopexy: the Colpopexy and Urinary Reduction Efforts (CARE) randomized surgical trial. *Int Urogynecol J Pelvic Floor Dysfunct.* 2008;19(5):607-614. doi:10.1007/s00192-007-0498-2

results.endpoint: Urodynamic stress incontinence without prolapse reduction
results.measure: Preoperative urodynamic stress incontinence without reduction, both arms combined

results.endpoint: Detection of urodynamic stress incontinence with reduction
results.measure: Leakage with prolapse reduction at 300 mL by method, both arms combined

results.endpoint: Postoperative stress incontinence by preoperative reduction test
results.measure: Stress incontinence at 3 months after a positive versus negative preoperative reduction stress test (either of two methods, 300 mL)
results.note: P = 0.19 with Burch and P = 0.04 without Burch. Burch lowered postoperative stress incontinence whether or not the reduction test showed leakage. The analysis predates the 2016 correction; the primary report gives 22.9% with Burch and 47.9% without among women with no leakage on reduction (P < 0.001, data not shown).

results.measure: Mesh or suture erosion within 2 years, all 322 participants
results.note: 20 (6%): 17 mesh and 3 suture; mean interval from surgery 313 days (range 45–744). No difference by randomized Burch.

results.measure: Odds of erosion with any ePTFE graft versus none
results.note: Erosion in 4/21 (19%) with ePTFE and 16/301 (5%) without.

results.measure: Odds of erosion with concurrent hysterectomy versus none
results.note: Concurrent hysterectomy in 60% of women with erosion versus 24% of those without.

results.measure: Odds of erosion with current smoking versus not
results.note: Current smoking in 5/20 (25%) with erosion versus 18/302 (6%) without.

harms.label: Mesh erosions treated with at least one operation
harms.note: Two resolved, 6 had persistent erosion and 5 were lost to follow-up; none of the 4 managed by observation resolved.

delivery.label: Graft material
delivery.value: Synthetic mesh in 92%: woven polyester 42%, polypropylene 48%, ePTFE 6%
delivery.note: Use of ePTFE was stopped for later participants on the safety board's instruction in February 2005.

delivery.label: Other concomitant procedures
delivery.value: Paravaginal repair 61/322 (18.9%); any culdoplasty 112/322 (34.8%); rectocele repair 78/322 (24.2%)

delivery.label: Vaginal graft sutures
delivery.note: A minimum of two stitches secured the graft to the sacrum.
